Label: ^specific gravity\b|^density\b
Note: a density's specimen form is rarely stated

Label: ^specific density\b|^dichte\b
Note: a maker may call it the specific density; purefil's German sheets print Dichte, and both are the row this database keeps as Density

Label: ^(printed part|material|filament) density\b
Note: a maker may say whose density the row is: BASF heads it Printed Part Density and Fillamentum Material density, and this database keeps one Density per grade

Label: ^strength\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: a row labelled only "Strength" under a tensile standard states no endpoint, which is the property this is

Label: ^stress at break\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the sheet names the endpoint and the method column names the tensile test; a stress the sheet states at an elongation is not this row and is left for the owner

Label: ^breaking stress\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the same row under the maker’s other name for it

Label: ^yield (stress|strength)\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the method column names the tensile test, so the yield is the tensile one

Label: ^streckspannung\b
Note: the stress at yield on a German sheet

Label: ^streckdehnung\b
Note: the strain at yield on a German sheet

Label: ^rei(ss|\u00df)dehnung\b
Note: the strain at break on a German sheet

Label: ^yield strain\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the strain at yield of a tensile test is the elongation at yield

Label: ^zug-?e-?modul\b
Note: purefil prints its German sheets with the German names; Zug-E-Modul is the tensile modulus

Label: ^e-?modulus\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?178|ASTM\s?D\s?790)\b)
Note: a sheet may head the row with the modulus alone; which modulus it is is the test it names, and ISO 178 is the bending test

Label: ^e-?modulus\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?527|ASTM\s?D\s?(?:638|882))\b)
Note: the same row where the test it names is the tensile one

Label: ^breaking elongation( rate)?\b
Note: Bambu heads the row Breaking Elongation Rate, which is the elongation at failure this database keeps

Label: ^(tensile )?elongation[^a-z]{0,3}\(?(at )?break|^tensile strain at break|^tensile elongation[^a-z]*(at )?break|^elongation[^a-z]*at break|^tensile strain \(break\)
^elongation at stren\w*
Note: a sheet spells it strenght; a source’s own typo is not a reason to lose the row

Label: ^flexural (strain|elongation)[^a-z]{0,3}\(?(at )?break
Note: BASF heads the row "Flexural Strain at Break" and "Flexural elongation at break", and properties.csv keeps one row for it; a bending strain is not the tensile elongation the row above matches

Label: ^flexular modulus
Note: a sheet spells it Flexular; a source's own typo is not a reason to lose the row

Label: ^flexular strength
Note: the same typo on the strength row

Label: ^charpy[^a-z]*(impact )?(strength )?(of )?notched|^notched charpy
Note: a sheet may put a word between the test and its notch: Charpy Impact Strength of Notched Specimen

Label: ^charpy
Note: an unqualified Charpy row is the unnotched one; the method may say otherwise and wins

Label: ^izod[^a-z]*(impact )?(strength )?(of )?notched|^notched izod
Note: the same row as the one above it: Izod Impact Strength of Notched Specimen

Label: ^notched impact strength\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?179|ISO\s?180|ASTM\s?D\s?256|GB\s?/\s?T\s?(?:1043|1843))\b)
Note: the row names the notch and not the test, and the method column names which test it is; a row that names no method is left to the label above it, which is where a sheet that prints a block per notch says Charpy or Izod

Label: ^un-?notched impact strength\b(?=.*\b(?:ISO\s?179|ISO\s?180|ASTM\s?D\s?256|GB\s?/\s?T\s?(?:1043|1843))\b)
Note: the same row unnotched

Label: ^(temperature of deflection under load|heat (deflection|distortion)( temp(erature)?)?\b|deflection temp(erature)?\b|hdt)
Note: the load is a condition the row or the line above states; a sheet may abbreviate it "Heat deflection temp." or print the abbreviation in place of the word: "Heat Distortion (HDT)"

Label: ^vicar
Note: Bambu spells it Vicar on every one of its forty-one sheets; a source's own typo is not a reason to lose the row

Label: ^melt(ing)? (temperature|point)|^melting temp\b
Note: a sheet may abbreviate it: Melting Temp.

Label: ^(equilibrium |saturated |saturation )?water absorption|^(equilibrium |saturated |saturation )?(moisture|humidity) absorption
Note: a sheet may call the equilibrium value the saturated one

Label: ^(shore|rockwell) hardness|^hardness|^shore [ad]\b
Note: the scale is part of the unit, and the sheet states it

Label: ^(thermal conductivity|w(ä|a)rmeleit(zahl|f(ä|a)higkeit)|conducibilit(à|a) termica|conductivit(é|e) thermique|conductividad t(é|e)rmica)
Note: purefil prints its sheets in four languages and its thermal conductivity row carries no value; unread, the row was claimed by the label above it and its 23 °C condition became a Vicat softening point

Label: ^(?:@\s?\d+\s?%\s?)?decomposition temp(erature)?\b
Note: a sheet may state the mass loss the temperature is read at (@5% Decomposition Temp.); that is the test's condition, not part of the value

Label: ^(mou?ld(ing)? |injection )?shrinkage\b|^schwindung\b
Note: a sheet may name the direction it measured in (flow direction, X/Y, Z), which is the row's own Direction; purefil prints Schwindung

Label: ^(specific )?surface resist(ance|ivity)\b
Note: a sheet may call it the surface resistance; properties.csv keeps the row in ohms either way

Label: ^(specific )?volume resist(ance|ivity)\b
Note: the same row through the body of the material

Label: ^tear (strength|resistance)\b
Note: the force per thickness that tears a specimen

Label: ^oxygen index\b|^limiting oxygen index\b|^\bLOI\b
Note: the least oxygen that sustains burning; it is a measurement, not the flammability class a sheet claims beside it

Label: ^compression set\b
Note: the time and temperature a sheet states beside it are the test's conditions

Label: ^poisson.?s? ?-? ?ratio\b
Note: a sheet may name the definition it used (acc. to Hencky), which is the method and not the value

Label: ^dielectric strength\b
Note: the thickness a sheet states beside it is the test's condition

Label: ^(relative permittivity|permittivity|dielectric constant)\b
Note: the frequency a sheet states beside it is the test's condition, not part of the value

Label: ^comparative tracking index\b|^\bCTI\b
Note: the voltage a wetted surface tracks at

Label: ^abrasion loss\b|^abrasion resistance\b
Note: the volume a standard abrasive removes; a sheet may head the row abrasion resistance and print the loss

Label: ^coefficient of (thermal|linear) exp(ansion)?\b|^cte\b
Note: a sheet may abbreviate it: Coefficient of Thermal Exp.

Label: ^contin[uo]*s (service|use|operating) temperature
Note: a sheet spells it Continous; a source's own typo is not a reason to lose the row

Label: ^low temperature impact( strength)?
Note: a maker's name for an impact test run below room temperature; which test it is comes from the standard it names, and the temperature is the row's own condition

Label: ^impact\b|^notched$|^unnotched$
Note: the sheet names no test; ISO 180 or ASTM D256 makes it Izod, ISO 179 or GB/T 1043 Charpy

Label: ^(?:tensile )?elongation\b(?!\s+at\s+tear\b)(?!\s*\((?!\s*(?:%|\d|X-?Y\b|Z\b|ISO|ASTM|DIN|EN\b|GB|at\b|break|yield|max)))|^ultimate elongation\b|^nominal (elongation|strain) at break\b|^strain at break\b
Note: an unqualified ISO 527 elongation is the value at failure, which is how this database records the sheets that print one figure; a sheet that labels its endpoint matches the row above this one. A qualifier the lexicon cannot read is not unqualified: Extrudr prints Tensile Elongation (Indentation Depth) 5 % on a sheet that also prints Nominal Elongation at Break > 50 %, and the two are not the same measurement
